memo.verdict: Park. Neutral-to-bearish on the case; conviction medium on the park and low on direction, because the shares are a geared option whose expected value is near zero with a wide skew either way, and the record would not short an option on a 10 percent float. The park rule applies in full and the record does not argue otherwise: management ('No mediocre management', RA 3, E 1, BB 4) D; business quality ('Business', E 2, BB 2) D; predictability ('Transmission', RA 8, E 2, BB 4) F; trackability ('Leading indicators', RA 7, E 2, BB 4) D. The condition that would re-open it: a binding e& PPF swap agreement with clearance filings and a published state-review outcome that leaves the HUF 1.3 trillion defence framework intact, together, with the shares at or below HUF 1,250; at that point the case would be re-sorted as 'Major CfC Clearing' with the clearing evidenced and the earnings path re-run. Not an invalidation: the option may pay at about one in four on the three conditions together; it is not a case the framework can underwrite at 20 percent a year.
case: The thesis as the record states it: 4iG is a transformation case that has not reached the shareholder. A founder-controlled Hungarian telecom-led conglomerate is re-plumbing itself through a holding structure (the four-pillar restructure of 15 January 2026), an infrastructure carve-out (One Magyarország from 2Connect), a share swap with e& PPF (49 percent of CETIN Hungary for 38 percent of 2Connect, cashless, up to EUR 1 billion of claimed synergies, non-binding term sheet, closing "by early 2027"), partner-funded defence and space pillars (CSG Defence's 49 percent of the defence sub-holding closed 2 September 2026; a HUF 1.3 trillion framework through 2035 signed in March 2026; EUR 3.5 billion committed backlog; EUR 4.5 billion of options; HUF 96 billion of private equity for HUSAT) and, from 27 August 2026, an energy pillar with wind assets and a non-binding nuclear letter of intent. The change has travelled through resources, choices and actions into revenue and stopped.

The chain, link by link. 'Change Forces' (E 1, BB 1) B: internal forces (RA 2) B because the screen's decision rule is met several times over, with three red flags firing (empire-building; dangerous leverage at 3.7x, BB−, a 5.0x covenant, unhedged euro debt; a 'PowerPoint' claim of HUF 400 billion of enterprise value "unlocked" and EUR 1 billion of synergies); external forces (RA 1) C because they are strong and net mixed, the defence tailwind acting on a sliver (1.7 percent of FY2025 segment revenue, about 11 percent of H1 2026 revenue), the telecom market flat, the tax tailwinds banked, and the political force (the review ordered 18 August 2026 by Prime Minister Péter Magyar, an 11 percent one-day fall) a headwind on the whole. Within the internal forces: strategy change B (re-articulated twice in 2026, resourced with partners' capital, contradicting itself in August); other leaders B (the bench rebuilt 15 January 2026; the last independent director gone 21 November 2025; no activist); new products B (Yettel on 2Connect since 1 July 2026 and Microsoft status since 16 July 2026 earning now; the rest investment); balance sheet D (fully used, direction down; the NKP II bullet bought time); acquisitions C (small and sensible in 2026; Vodafone Hungary at 9.1 times EBITDAaL on Deutsche Bank's figure, "a 50 percent premium" on Morgan Stanley's); perimeter C (reduced in the right places, widened in the wrong ones); shareholder returns F (no dividend since FY2021; the only "buyback" was HUF 7,083 million of executives' shares bought by a subsidiary at HUF 3,446.80 in January 2026); chief executive D (no change; an unchecked founder); standards D; guidance D (a revenue floor "above 10 percent", a 4.0x ceiling, HUF 150 billion of network investment to 2028, nothing on earnings); price rises D (a voluntary freeze through H1 2026 while Magyar Telekom raised 4.4 percent); new geographies C; catch-all D (Mubadala's dilutive deleveraging; insiders taking cash out).

'Financial Outputs' (E 2, BB 1) D: only revenue is improving. Key metrics (RA 2) D: revenue growth B (8.5 percent FY2025 to 16.7 percent H1 2026); margin F (EBITDA margin 34.9 to 30.9 percent; EBIT −16.82 percent on revenue +16.69 percent; "operating leverage failed to materialize"); cash conversion D (not computable on a loss; free cash flow down 10 percent; HUF 39 billion absorbed in working capital; parent cash HUF 4,533 million); net debt D (3.2x to 3.7x in six months). Goldilocks growth (RA 3) F: EPS negative in the base and in modal FY2026 (HUF −25 underlying), so no rate exists for six or eighteen months and the three-year rate (adjusted HUF 22 to HUF 136) is off an add-back base; the metric is the finding and is kept because free cash flow per share would also be near zero and would hide the minority leakage. Sell-side upgrades (RA 1) F: no consensus, no earnings guidance, and the research's direction down. Staircase (RA 4) B: one of the longest in the universe (the swap by early 2027; the 2Connect 11 percent sale; Starlink Mobile by 2027; REMTECH from late 2026; Poli Computer from 1 October 2026; Tábori as Group Vice Chairman from 1 January 2027; Nasdaq in Q4 2027; Mubadala 2029; HUGEO 2030; nine HUSAT satellites by 2032), not A because the two steps the market most needs (the swap closing; the review closing) are the two the company controls least.
counter_case: At its strongest, 4iG is a sum-of-the-parts story in which the market, after a 68 percent fall driven by politics and a diversification it disliked, is capitalising a HUF 300-billion-EBITDA Hungarian telecom operator with a 42,000 km wholesale backbone a competitor already pays for, a 30 percent active mobile share and a telecom EBITDA margin of 40 to 48 percent at 5.6 times group EBITDA, below the only CEE transaction precedent in the research (7.7 to 9.1 times for Vodafone Hungary), with a EUR 3.5 billion committed defence backlog, a USD 100 million Axiom Space stake and a 38 percent Rába interest thrown in. The e& PPF swap will put a transaction mark on 2Connect within six months; a UAE sovereign fund will pay for 11 percent of it; the proceeds deleverage; Scope's BB− has held through the December 2025 allegations and the August 2026 review; the forint's post-election strength keeps shrinking the euro debt, and the HUF 36 billion of H1 2026 currency gains are a real reduction in a real euro liability; the defence backlog is one nobody is modelling because nobody covers the stock; the Nasdaq plan brings a buyer base that does not read Hungarian politics; the company has closed every transaction it announced in 2026; and the dashboard's interest level is A. A one-and-a-half-turn re-rating of the enterprise multiple adds about half to the share price, because the equity is 31 percent of the enterprise value and the gearing that has already cut the shares one way cuts them back the other. The staircase of dated events is one of the longest in the universe. The Hungarian triopoly is benign, the incumbent is raising prices, the sector taxes are gone, Yettel chose to rent rather than build, and the telecom sub-holding's foundations are the strongest in the CEE cohort outside Magyar Telekom's; the holding's losses are the cost of a defence and space option that partners now fund, and once the energy pillar is ring-fenced the shareholder owns a strong operator with a cheap option attached. Reviews of this kind in Hungary end in renegotiation, not cancellation, because the state co-owns 37.9 percent of the asset and the systems are embedded; the swap closes by early 2027; when both happen the clearing is sudden and the stock does not wait, so this is a 'Major CfC Clearing' case in waiting whose price has already done the capitulating. And the framework's riskiness and simplicity tests are built for Western compounders and will always fail a CEE national champion, so the asymmetric opportunity sits precisely where the framework's tests fail; at −68 percent from the high the risks are paid for.

What the record concedes: the enterprise multiple is below the one precedent; the swap would be a real mark; the gearing cuts both ways and the market has already cut it one way; the staircase is long; the forint has been a tailwind and may stay one; the telecom foundation is genuinely strong and the partners' capital keeps the parent's cash untouched; the price has capitulated; and the framework is built for a different kind of company.
triggers: - Re-open the case: a binding swap agreement with Hungarian and Austrian clearance filings and a published review outcome leaving the HUF 1.3 trillion framework intact, together, with the shares at or below HUF 1,250; then re-sort as 'Major CfC Clearing' and re-run the earnings path.

- Odds that would move: a signed, binding swap moves (a) from plausible to probable; a stated policy of using the stake-sale proceeds to deleverage at group level moves (b) to probable; a published review outcome settles (c) either way; a FY2026 attributable profit excluding currency and amortisation above zero moves (e) to likely.

- Alarm levels: net debt to EBITDA above 3.9x; EUR/HUF above 400; the EBITDA margin below 30 percent for a full year; any state cancellation or re-pricing of a framework; a Scope outlook change to negative.

- Invalidate levels: net debt to EBITDA above 4.0x; a Scope downgrade to B+; cancellation of the HUF 1.3 trillion framework; the swap abandoned; attributable profit excluding currency and amortisation negative for FY2027.

- Near steps to watch (within six months): Q3 2026 results; the Poli Computer merger (1 October 2026); the first Yettel wholesale revenue through 2Connect; the Hungarian wind portfolio closing (49 percent of 158 MW); the swap's competition filings; the EU Council decision on EUR 4.2 billion of cohesion funds; the review's first findings.

- The eleven leading indicators: EUR/HUF; the swap filings; the review announcements; Scope's actions; NMHH quarterly mobile shares; quarterly EBITDA margin by pillar (telecom above 40 percent, group above 33 percent); net debt to EBITDA (towards 3.5x); attributable profit ex currency and amortisation (positive by FY2027); 2Connect wholesale revenue; IT recurring share (55 percent); the cohesion-fund decision; insider-dealing announcements. Only the currency and the share price are monthly or better.
